source.author: A. A. Steiner
source.title: A universal method for preparing nutrient solutions of a certain desired composition
source.provenance: Article text supplied by the user; page and figure interpretations cross-checked in the Steiner scientific audit. Transcribed ambiguities are retained, not silently corrected.

experimental_design.qualification: 20 x 16 x 5 = 1600 nominal conditions at the main strength. The later printed 360 conflicts with 320; another 80 intermediate combinations are mentioned. Do not invent a resolved total or count all nominal conditions as successful reformulated batches. Already turbid mixtures and those precipitating during KOH titration were excluded from reformulation. No case-level dataset or replication statistics is supplied.

figure_6.ordinate: Added OH equivalents as a percentage of total phosphate on the H2PO4 reporting basis
figure_6.qualification: The paper compares solution 1a to curve A despite the ratio-label mismatch. Preserve that comparison without treating it as a resolved mapping or an independent holdout validation. Figure 6 base-dose percentages are not the HPO4 species fraction from Figure 1.

worked_example.qualification: The stated approximately 6.37 after aeration is a worked-example expectation, not a reported measured batch result or a FlahaX prediction.

water_conductivity.qualification: The usual value and printed inequality are internally inconsistent. Do not reverse the inequality or derive an accepted water conductivity limit.

concentration_basis.definition: Sum of six analytical nutrient amounts K, Ca, Mg, nitrate, total phosphate and sulfate; not mass of fertilizer salts.
concentration_basis.electroneutrality_basis: Full actual aqueous species, not equality of the two independently normalized nutrient subsets

higher_strength_observation.qualification: Only a few combinations reported feasible; above pH 6.5 very few extreme ratios remain. This is not general method validation at 42 mmol/L.

historical_domain.upper_limit_qualification: Upper pH coverage varies by K:Ca curve and feasible composition; no universal upper cutoff is inferred from the precision statements.

ph_precision.range_description: above pH 7.0, within feasible curve coverage

historical_domain.precision_scope: Author-reported historical method precision, not a confidence interval, instrument uncertainty, FlahaX prediction bound or acceptance tolerance. Shared band endpoints do not establish a new sharper boundary rule.
exclusions: combinations precipitating even inside the drawn curve range

additional_ions.Na: exploratory K+Na substitution in the curve ratio; not demonstrated nutritional equivalence

historical_domain.qualification: Being at 30 mmol/L and within a quoted precision band does not establish applicability to every ratio or pH. The article does not establish crop optima, crop sufficiency, phase-specific kinetics or universal physical stability.

empirical_screens.threshold_description: above 60 reported infeasible, independent of pH in the study
empirical_screens.unit_interpretation: Dimensional interpretation when both input concentrations are mmol/L; the printed product unit is inconsistent.

empirical_screens.threshold_description: approximately 2.2 doubtful; above it turbidity reported, with composition-dependent borderline cases
empirical_screens.unit_interpretation: Dimensional interpretation when both input concentrations are mmol/L; the printed product unit is inconsistent.
empirical_screens.phosphate_fraction_method: Approximate Figure 1 graphical HPO4 fraction of total phosphate at the relevant pH; not Figure 6 OH dose fraction

screen_scope: Historical concentration-product screens are contextual empirical evidence, not activity-based mineral saturation indices, universal solubility constants or guarantees of retained dissolved nutrients.
